what_happened.line: The Board of Selectmen voted unanimously the previous night to certify a design enrollment for the new school, the building committee chair reported.
No date was set for the special vote; the building committee is leaning toward January over December.
The building committee chair said the MSBA support rate is expected to be closer to the higher of two figures.
The superintendent said the October 1 enrollment count is significant for state reporting and funding.
The committee decided no business beyond adjournment; no votes were taken and no one spoke in public comment.

why_it_matters: The certified design enrollment sets the size the state will help pay for, and the state's support rate and the timing of the special vote shape what residents will be asked to approve for the new school and how much falls on local taxes.
The state does not build for non-resident choice students, so choice openings affect how enrollment is counted as the new building approaches.
watch_next: The date of the special vote on the new school, which the building committee is leaning toward holding in January rather than December.
